not_verified: DEFECT 7 COULD NOT BE PROVEN IN A BROWSER, only in jsdom. It needs one surface that has BOTH meta.row_total AND a live cross-filter, and today none does: row_total is emitted by m02/m03/m04/m06/m16 and the only surface with a live cross-filter is m12 (m04/m06/m16 were switched off by declaration in the reconcile round). Checkable the day an RPC gives a row_total surface a chart.filter_key. The code path itself is covered by the new ReportSurface test.

DEFECT 4 IS RENDERER-ONLY UNTIL THE RPC DECLARES IT. Measured this turn on the live payload (report_m20_satisfaction_g3_post_baseline.json): none of m20's four charts carries a layout key, so the screen still draws vertical bars. The RPC owner adds layout: 'horizontal' to the two reason charts and nothing else changes. My horizontal path is covered by fixtures only - it has never rendered in a real browser, so the measured 6.6px-per-character axis width is an ESTIMATE (jsdom cannot measure text) and should be eyeballed once a real payload declares it.

THE AXIS FORMATTER IS ONLY AS GOOD AS WHAT THE PAYLOAD DECLARES, and most live payloads declare a display string, not a C8 format enum. Measured over 126 payload files: chart.unit is '₪' x51, 'משובים' x42, '%' x18, 'הערות' x14, 'ציון' x8 ... against 'money' x15 / 'percent' x15 / 'int' x4; series[].format is null in 296 of 342 series. Consequence seen live: m20's 'satisfied share by year' axis reads 0/25/50/75/100 with NO % sign, because its unit is the literal '%' rather than 'percent'. The defect as reported (raw 600000) is fixed either way - the fallback groups digits - but the unit suffix needs a one-word RPC change (chart.unit: 'percent', or declare series[].format). I did NOT map '%'/'₪' to formats in the client: that would be a second convention beside the C8 enum, i.e. exactly the two-mechanisms-for-one-behaviour class the reconcile round removed. Conflict question, not a patch (C7).

blind_spot: The 0-count rule (defect 6) is a GUESS ABOUT THE ROWS made from the CHART, and nothing checks the guess. ChartCard cannot see payload.rows, so 'this column would filter to nothing' is approximated by 'every series value on this datum is 0'. The two are not the same set. Concretely checkable in one step: open /reports?tab=finance&report=equipment as CEO and click the shortest bar of 'הוזמן מול הגיע' - if a datum with a NON-zero chart value still filters the table to zero rows, the user gets an enabled bar, a pointer cursor and an empty table, which is precisely the state the card wanted marked not-allowed; and the mirror case is a datum whose chart value is 0 for the plotted series while rows for that category do exist (a stacked chart whose plotted series is not the one the rows count), where my rule now DISABLES a filter that would have worked. Neither case exists in today's payloads - m12's bars are all non-zero and m20's single 0 category has no rows - which is exactly why no test of mine catches it. The durable fix is for ReportSurface (which holds both sides) to compute selectability from the rows and pass it to ChartCard, instead of ChartCard inferring it from the bar height; I did not do that because it changes the ChartCard prop contract that four tab owners are building against, and the brief said every change additive.
